construction.note: The triangles, hexagon and channel lines follow Charlotte Webb’s ATM handout. The work log records first-try matches of those drawings and the final motif.
construction.changes: App step 7 replaces the handout’s suggested large-hexagon repeat with a smaller hexagon. This is an intentional correction made to match the tilework photo, so the complete lesson is an adaptation.

credits.source: Art in the Mathematics Classroom: Islamic Geometry (ATM conference handout)
credits.creator: Charlotte Webb
credits.note: The construction pictures are on PDF pages 12–13. The sequence of two triangles, the hexagon, and lines through the triangles' crossings carried to the hexagon follows the handout's six-fold construction. The handout repeats the large hexagon; the real tilework repeats the smaller hexagon of step 7 instead.

credits.source: Computer Graphics and Geometric Ornamental Design, chapter 3
credits.creator: Craig S. Kaplan
credits.note: Describes this pattern as six-pointed stars placed in a tiling of hexagons, which confirmed the repeat used here.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the radius of the first circle, and the unit for every length.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A. Keep this compass size until the end.
Draw a circle with centre A through O. Draw a circle with centre D through O, where the line crosses the first circle on the left. The two new circles touch at O.

Draw a circle with centre B through O. Draw a circle with centre C through O. Draw a circle with centre E through O. Draw a circle with centre F through O. B, C, E and F are where the two new circles cross the first one. Six circles now ring the first circle.
Join A, C and E with straight lines. Join B, D and F with straight lines. The two triangles make a six-pointed star. They cross at K1 to K6.
Join A, B, C, D, E and F with straight lines. This hexagon frames the drawing.
Draw a straight line through K1 and K3, K3 and K5, K5 and K1, and K2 and K4. Draw a straight line through K4 and K6, and K6 and K2. These lines make a smaller star. They run on to the hexagon.

parts.text: Draw a straight line through K1 and R12. It crosses the horizontal line at T. T is the middle of the small hexagon at A.
Turn T round O by 60°, five times, to get the other corners of the tile. Join the six points: this small hexagon is the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink six small hexagons, one at each corner of the large hexagon. The six-pointed star is left between them.

parts.text: Ink the small hexagon at A: from A through R1, K1, J1, K6 and R12, back to A.
Ink the same small hexagon at B, C, D, E and F. Tick “Also ink the copies round the centre” to ink them all at once.

pattern.text: Put copies of the tile side by side. Each corner hexagon is completed by the tiles that share it. Every hexagon touches three stars.

expect.note: Golden values, in units of OA, computed by the engine and checked for six-fold symmetry, no slivers, and pieces that exactly fill the tile. The hexagons have side 1/3 and the star's points reach 1/√3.
